definition: A plural pronoun meem followed by a moving letter that is not a hamza may be read as in Hafs with a sukun, or joined with a waw of two harakat.
limitations: Paraphrase of the cited pages by an automated drafter; not scholarly reviewed.
Only Book A is cited; the printed page is where the section begins and needs proofreading.
Both readings are listed in `variants`; the meem carries no sign in the corpus.

Before ba and meem the corpus writes the sakin meem with no sukun (as for ikhfa and idgham shafawi). Those places are included: p.17 says the sila applies to a plural meem before any moving letter that is not a hamza, and p.18 gives an example before a meem (في قلوبهم مرض); no example is given before a ba, so that case rests on the general wording. Their `variants` are the same as the older places, ["iskan", "sila_2_harakat"]: p.17 says the sila of the plural meem is « قدر حركتين ».

The book does not say how the sila relates to ikhfa or idgham shafawi. By the construction of the rule, with the sila the meem is no longer sakin, so ikhfa/idgham shafawi on the same meem apply to the iskan reading only. This is an inference recorded in the notes of both annotations, not a statement of the book.

conditions.description: A final sakin meem of the plural pronoun (hum, kum, tum).
